prompt:
Write 11 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim, in time order. Injury: neck strain. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1356; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- The patient was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that condition adds to the current complaints.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant later added small details, but the account stayed the same.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received by phone from the claimant, who reports a low-speed collision while backing out of a space in a parking lot. The claimant is not represented by counsel and is handling the matter directly.

Entry 2: Reviewed the policy file and confirmed the driver is named on the policy and coverage was in force at the time of the loss. No prior claims or gaps in coverage appear on the record.

Entry 3: Obtained the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the incident and notes the reporting officer's observations at the scene.

Entry 4: Contacted the other driver, who confirms the accident happened as the claimant described it. Witness statements received so far are consistent with that account.

Entry 5: Received photographs of both vehicles from the scene. Damage to the rear bumper and tailgate of the claimant's vehicle lines up well with the impact described.

Entry 6: Requested maintenance and prior repair history for the vehicle. No earlier damage to the same areas is known, and nothing in the records suggests the damage predates the coverage start.

Entry 7: Claimant reported neck pain and stiffness the day after the collision and provided initial medical records. The kind and force of the impact are a reasonable match for the reported injury.

Entry 8: Reviewed prior medical records. The claimant was treated for the same body area within the last two years, and that earlier condition adds to the current complaints, so it will be factored into the evaluation.

Entry 9: Claimant later supplied a few additional details about the seating position and the moment of impact. These are minor and do not change the core account, which has stayed consistent from the first report.

Entry 10: Treatment followed a usual course, with physical therapy and follow-up visits. Symptoms have been tapering as the claimant improves, and the most recent treatment notes reflect steady progress.

Entry 11: Based on the documented damage, witness and police confirmation, medical course, and the claimant's consistent account, the file is ready for evaluation. The prior body-area history will be noted in the injury assessment.
